acceptance: The measurement method and figures are recorded so the problem can be re-measured.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
Against one baseline, the median normalized ratio differs by GitHub runner class from about 1.04 to about 1.23, and the same head has scored 1.010 and 1.238 (#4351) and 1.080 and 1.287 (#4311) on different runners. Across 55 runs the coefficient of variation of the normalized ratio is 0.085 with the CPU-calibration normalizer. Within one runner class, shared-test slowdown is 0.7 to 0.9 points a day. Most false blocks come from runner class, not baseline age. Dividing by collection time lowers the variation to 0.026 but lets a pull request influence its own divisor and loosens with suite growth, so it is not proposed; the owner's decision on that work is pending in duration-gate-redesign-prs-owner-decision-20261120.

## Change
No fix is proposed. Keep the data (scripts and inputs are not committed; record the method here) and bring options to the owner if false blocks recur.

## Decision gates
Any normalizer or threshold change is an owner decision (the owner decided on 2026-11-17: no threshold change).

## Verification rubric
Pass: the method to reproduce the per-class medians and the variation figure from CI artifacts is written on this item.

## Additions from the item review
- Copy /tmp/fdrc* to a durable location outside the repository before cleanup. Re-open this question on any would-block that passes on a full re-run.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
